title: The Floating Act
summary: Saw a magnet, wind a hidden coil and wire its battery so a ring magnet floats at the ribbon in a stage magic show.
subject: physics
concepts: Every piece of a magnet is a weaker whole magnet
Right-hand rule for the north pole
learningOutcome: The student can say which pole a sawn face becomes and what moment a piece has, find a coil’s moment m = NIA and its north end, and wind a coil that matches a bar magnet.

levels.title: Saw the magnet
levels.adds: Baseline: every piece of a magnet is a whole magnet, cut across or along, never a lone pole (Example 5.1); a k/12 piece has k/12 of the moment.
hints: Every piece has its own N and S: a sawn face becomes the pole opposite to the end it faces.
The piece points the same way as the bar, whatever colour its paint is.
A piece of k/12 of the bar has k/12 of its magnetic moment.

levels.title: The hidden coil
levels.adds: New idea: a coil is a magnet with m = NIA, no iron needed, and the right-hand rule gives its north end (Ex 5.3).
hints: m = N I A, so N = m/(IA), with the area in m².
Curl your right hand’s fingers along the current in the front turns: the thumb points to N.
Like poles must face each other for the ring to float.

levels.title: Swap a magnet for a coil
levels.adds: More steps: a coil with the same moment as a bar magnet makes the same field; change the turn area from cm² to m² (Section 5.2.2).
hints: Same moment, same field: the coil needs the magnet’s m.
Put the magnet’s top pole on top of the coil, using the right-hand rule.

misconceptions: Cutting a bar magnet separates the north and south poles
A piece cut from the north half of a magnet is all north
A solenoid has a magnetic moment only if it has an iron core
A thinner magnet cut along its length has a single pole
